original_value: Persistent surveillance is one of the major tasks envisioned for unmanned aerial vehicles in that some regions of interest need to be continuously surveyed. This distinction from the one-time coverage/exploration does not allow a straightforward application of the most exploration techniques to address the persistent surveillance problem. This article introduces and demonstrates a method of alterable artificial potential field to control a group of unmanned aerial vehicles to stay over the region of interest. We present attractive potential field to drive the unmanned aerial vehicles to desirable areas, obstacle potential field to move away from obstacles, collision avoidance potential field to control unmanned aerial vehicles not to collide with others, and formation of potential field to make unmanned aerial vehicles gather in a group. The simulation results show that the proposed approach could generate collision-free path for unmanned aerial vehicles staying over the region of interest for a long endurance.

result.paraphrase: Persistent surveillance is a major envisioned task for unmanned aerial vehicles because some regions of interest must be monitored continuously. Unlike one-time coverage or exploration, this difference means most exploration techniques cannot be directly applied to the persistent surveillance problem. This article introduces and demonstrates an adaptive artificial potential field method for controlling a group of unmanned aerial vehicles to remain over the region of interest. We describe an attractive potential field to guide the aircraft to desired areas, an obstacle potential field to steer them away from obstacles, a collision-avoidance potential field to prevent them from colliding with one another, and a formation potential field to bring the aircraft together as a group. Simulation results show that the proposed approach can generate collision-free paths for unmanned aerial vehicles staying over the region of interest for a long endurance.
